nh_illmob_boulder_the.blurb: A single boulder in the Boulder Natural section of Pawtuckaway State Park, tucked in the forest beside the trail near the start of the walk-in. It holds eleven problems from V0 up to V7, spread fairly evenly through the easy and middle grades, with one hard sloper test-piece at the top end. Because so many lines sit close together, it works as a small circuit with plenty of linkups. The easy problems make it a decent place for newer boulderers to spend a day, and stronger climbers can use it to warm up. It is often overlooked in favour of busier boulders nearby, and the surrounding woods are shady.

nh_the_buttermilk_boulder.blurb: One of the better-known boulders in the Boulder Natural section of Pawtuckaway State Park, a short way north of the Zoo. Its tall front face has a flake running up the middle and draws steady traffic from climbers warming up or looking for a challenge. The stream side offers two demanding aretes and a difficult sit-start linkup, while the steeper back has entry-level moderates. The eleven problems run from V0 to V6, weighted toward the easy end, with a handful in the middle grades. Expect crowds and a patchwork of crash pads around the landing on busy days.

nh_conditions_boulder.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in the Blair Woods section of Pawtuckaway State Park, on a hilltop beyond the Swirley Boulder. The eleven granite problems stretch from a V0 crack to a few very hard testpieces in the V8 to V10 range, though most of the lines in between sit around V3 to V5, including a popular classic. Other boulders lie close by, and a few more problems are still waiting to be cleaned. Blair Woods in general sees few crowds, so this corner tends to be quiet, and the short uphill walk from the main trail keeps it peaceful.

nh_falcon_wall.blurb: A north-facing sport wall on the ridge above Franconia Notch, a bit beyond the Eaglet spire. It offers a limited number of sustained, hard lines: eleven bolted routes from the 5.10 range through 5.13, with four at 5.12 and three at 5.13 making up most of the top end. Bolts are stainless. The walk in is a real hike of roughly half an hour or more, heading past the Eaglet and then onto a trail branching off to the right. Expect wet or dirty holds, bugs and changeable mountain weather, so it suits strong, patient sport climbers more than beginners.

nh_the_balcony_2.blurb: A large cliff high on the hill at Russell Crags in Merriam Woods, near Woodstock. Long lines on well-defined features give it an airy, exposed feel. Most of the eleven routes are bolted, with one trad line and one aid line mixed in, and grades run from 5.9 up to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 band. The walk up from the lower crags takes around half an hour and involves some route-finding past other walls, so it is a committed destination rather than a quick stop. Better for climbers comfortable on steadier, harder sport leads.

nh_storybrooke_bouldering.blurb: A small pocket of boulders and short routes in Russell Forest, between Russell Crags and Russell Pond near Woodstock. The five boulder problems all fall around V1 to V2 and make a pleasant little circuit, with the lines spaced within a few dozen feet of the trail. Alongside them are several short sport routes that run from easy grades up to about 5.10. It is only a couple of minutes from the car on a flagged trail with steep spots and downed trees, so it fits an easy, low-key outing or a warm-up before the bigger crags nearby. Russell Forest as a whole is wooded and quiet.

nh_upper_upper_cliffs.blurb: A tier of cliffs perched above the main Upper Cliff at Pawtuckaway State Park. Most of the eleven climbs are traditional lines, running from easy fifth class through the 5.5 to 5.9 range, with a couple of harder ones near 5.10 and 5.12 and a single hard boulder problem. The walk starts on the descent trail at the right end of the Upper Cliff and continues past its top, then follows ledges to a big flake. It is very rarely climbed, so expect quiet and less-traveled rock, and bring your own judgment on route-finding and protection.
